title: Kirkwood council to form subcommittee on revamped noise ordinance
text:
← Back to the wire

Kirkwood council to form subcommittee on revamped noise ordinance
Council members said a draft decibel-limit ordinance needs expert input before it is finalized, while agreeing the Billy G's noise complaints can be handled through existing special use permits.
The Kirkwood City Council agreed during a work session to explore forming a subcommittee to continue work on a proposed noise ordinance rather than vote on the draft that night.
THE MEETING The work session took place Thursday, October 1, 2026. Council attorney Darren presented a redlined draft that added a table of decibel limits measured either at the receiving property or the emitting property, along with proposed changes to nighttime hours.
DISAGREEMENT OVER APPROACH A council member said the ordinance should focus on what can actually be enforced. "So, I would just ask that then we focus on what's enforceable and that we're putting things in that are enforceable," the member said, noting no one was present to speak to enforcement.
A council member identified as Deb raised concerns about the scope of the rewrite. "I don't think we have an acoustical engineer on staff," she said, adding, "I don't think this ordinance is in a place yet for us to spend a lot of time on to really make these kinds of decisions."
Another council member pushed back on the pace of deliberation. "I think we're splitting hairs. I think we're overkilling this thing personally right now," the member said, arguing the council should focus instead on current noise problems near Billy G's.
THE SUBCOMMITTEE IDEA A council member proposed convening a focused work session. "Is there a way we can't put together a 4 hour, 6 hour, 8 hour work session that brings in an expert that se your selection of people who sit in there and pound it out and get it done?" the member asked, suggesting a subcommittee take on the task.
Darren offered to email a list of recommended changes as a starting point. The council agreed the Billy G's situation could be addressed in the meantime through the special use permit process rather than the new ordinance.
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT Council members said they would continue discussion at a future work session, with the subcommittee idea left for further development rather than formal action that night.
